name: proteomics_search
note: Unlike the prediction-item tasks, this is scored by RUNNING the search pipeline on real data and measuring two axes on the same runs. No predictions.jsonl / no LLM judge.

targets.speed: >= 5x faster end-to-end than the brute-force (Comet) baseline
targets.calibration: measured entrapment FMR <= 1.3% at claimed 1% FDR

phase1_breadth.note: Same 3-arm head-to-head (Comet vs Sage vs Sage+Mokapot), identical FASTA-build / tolerances / mods / uniform 1% FDR scorer, re-run on additional real PXD datasets. Every figure traces to a real scored run at s3://biomate-nextflow-work/proteomics_breadth_20261001/<dsid>/results/scored/metrics.json plus per-arm *.time.txt wall-clocks.
datasets_scored: species-mix (PXD028735, E. coli sample vs human+E.coli DB, tryptic)

generalized_ranges.speed_tryptic_sage_vs_comet_end_to_end: 2.7x (species-mix) to 5.3x (ProteomeTools) faster across the three tryptic datasets
generalized_ranges.calibration: every arm on every dataset entrapment-clean (measured FMR <= nominal at 1% operating point)

phase1_breadth.honest_variation: The no-enzyme HLA search is where rescoring gains are largest (+359% peptides, Mokapot lever +12.9%) but where Sage's speed edge inverts (844.5s vs Comet 217.4s, due to the 376M-fragment no-enzyme index). The Mokapot lever is small on clean tryptic runs (HeLa +0.4%, species-mix +2.1%) and large on hard/ambiguous spaces.

species_mix_PXD028735.regime: 2-species specificity: pure E. coli sample searched against a human+E.coli combined target DB (24,962 target -> 99,848 searched seqs)
species_mix_PXD028735.species_specificity_at_1pct: 97.3% of accepted peptides (7,679/7,890) attributed to E. coli, 2.67% (211) to human -- correct localization, no human-protein inflation

tools_attribution: Sage (Lazear, JPR 2023, MIT); Mokapot (Fondrie & Noble, Apache-2.0); OpenMS/Comet (Apache/BSD). BioMate composes/runs/benchmarks; it did not author these tools.
caveats: Phase-1 breadth now scored on 3 real datasets (ProteomeTools + HeLa + HLA); gains are strong but vary honestly by regime (see phase1_breadth).
The headline 3-arm table above is the ProteomeTools baseline; HeLa/HLA relative gains are in phase1_breadth and report §3.2.
Speed is not uniform: Sage is 2.7-5.3x faster on tryptic searches but slower than Comet on the no-enzyme HLA immunopeptidome (large-index trade for a big recall gain).
Absolute counts track data scale (deep HeLa ~25k peptides; synthetic ProteomeTools hundreds); relative gains between arms are the load-bearing result.
RAM measured the docker wrapper, not the tool.
